ME= myalgic encephalomyelitis (Also known as ME/CFS)

#myalgicencephalomyelitis #SevereME #MECFS #LongCovid #ChronicIllness 

Video description: a white woman with glasses and her hair in 2 plaits talks to the screen from her bed. She wears a blue t-shirt and there is a bat squishmallow stuffed down the bed behind her
bearsandbestfriends
 
4d
I love that you were able to go to the woods. No one has the right to question that. But also no one knows how long you had to reserve tiny bubbles of energy to be able to do that or how long it will take to get those tiny bubbles back again. Why would anyone question that?
Like
Reply
burgess.tracey6
 
4d
I get you totally Fran. Everyone's situation is different & after a while I think we adjust to take account of where we estimate the edge of our energy capacity is. I don't discuss much about my fluctuating health issues anymore, as it's too frustrating & upsetting. I'm able to work part time & that has to be my focus. But it's exhausting & anything else gets the scraps. All we can do is manage as best as we can. 💙💕
Like
Reply
nantes_accessibilite
 
6d
Honestly it shocks me you have to prove yourself. It shocks me even more that people will judge you on one or two videos of two minutes. What about the 23 hours and 56 minutes of the reste of your day? They just don’t see you. So they can judge. 🤨

Hope you can go to enjoy forest again without paying such a price. 🌲

I find the policing that goes on in the ME community rather curious. I don’t see this kind of questioning happening with other chronic illness groups. postvak_tanja
 
1w
Wtf is wrong with people?? I dont have MCAS but I do have moderate ME and I can tolerate make-up and some perfumes. The ME community is now policing our appearance? "You dont look sick" is exactly the judgement from healthy people including doctors that we have to be subjected to, we dont need it from other ME sufferers- Its not a competition and the goal is to get WELL , not to virtue signal any suffering we have. Omg!!

karpydm
 
1w
It affects everyone in such different ways. It's a spectrum of symptoms and severity and it ebbs and flows. Severity fluctuates. Symptoms fluctuate. ❤️
Like
Reply
themme_fatale
 
1w
There’s already so much suffering with this disease, it’s cooked that anyone is made to spend the precious energy they do have justifying themselves. You’re always so open about your experiences and fluctuations and personally I am so grateful and have learned a lot from you!

I’m so glad you’ve been able to do something nice, I hope any dip is as short as possible you get many more trips to the woods 💕
9 likes
Reply
jessicajaponica
 
1w
This was me in my late teens, fluctuating between occasionally moderate and mostly severe. Comments people made did so much damage to me, especially when they came from other people with M.E. I didn’t know about pacing back then, either (now I do and I’m still rubbish at it!).
Now, I’m very severe and worsening and I get the same sort of comments from my carers, which do just as much harm.
This is such a helpful video ☺️ I wish 18/19yo me could have seen it. Thank you for saying it 🫶🏻
It was lovely to see you make it to the woods. Hope the memories sustain you and wishing you more improved days to come.
Like
Reply
westaussi
 
1w
Honestly, the relentless drag of feeling insulted all the time, is a huge energy burden within itself.
Like
Reply
bean.and.bear.boutique
 
1w
Oh goodness! Do not apologise for posting your happy moments - they are the things which allow us to continue living. Recognise that these comments came from a place of envy and you’ll be able to pity the person who felt the need to rain on your sunshine.
Finally, severity labels do not have clear edges. It’s much more like a colour wheel than coloured blocks. We know what red is and what orange is - but at what point does red become orange?
